title: Keyboard input goes to the first Sticky Note instead of the clicked note in a wide panel
line: The reporter's open MR !1223 makes typing go into the clicked Sticky Note in a thick panel; verified on the rig.
explanation: Panels refuse keyboard focus until a widget asks for AcceptingInputStatus, but an inline Sticky Note only asked for it after it already had active focus, which it can never get first. So typing into a clicked note went to KRunner, and once the panel did take input it focused its first item, so later typing landed in the first note. The reporter's MR !1223 asks for input on press before forcing focus on the clicked editor, keeps it while that editor has focus, and releases it a turn later so switching between notes doesn't drop it.

commits.message:
notes: acquire panel input before focusing inline editors

Request panel keyboard interactivity before focusing a clicked inline note.
Retain accepting-input status for the focused inline editor and defer only
releasing the previous editor's status when focus changes between notes.

Keep saving synchronous before the inactive text binding restores noteText,
and exclude compact popup editors from panel input acquisition.

BUG: 527546

media.caption: Pure master, right panel 200 px with three inline notes: click note 2 and type MARK2, note 3 and MARK3, note 1 and MARK1.
Same steps with MR !1223: each text goes into the clicked note.
After clicking note 2 and typing MARK2: the text opened KRunner, the note stayed empty.
With the MR: MARK2 is in note 2.
Panel after typing into notes 2, 3 and 1: MARK3 and MARK1 both ended up in the first note.
With the MR: MARK2, MARK3 and MARK1 are each in the note that was clicked.

reviews.text: Requesting AcceptingInputStatus on press before forceActiveFocus and deferring status release on focus loss is the right approach in applets/notes/qml/main.qml to solve the panel focus chicken-and-egg issue. However, queueing an anonymous arrow function in Qt.callLater inside onActiveFocusChanged is unsafe if the note is destroyed while focused (e.g., via the delete button), since anonymous callbacks are not cancelled on item destruction and can dereference a destroyed mainTextArea/Plasmoid. In addition, setting AcceptingInputStatus on right-click before opening the separate contextMenu window can leave Plasmoid.status stuck at AcceptingInputStatus if the unfocused note never transitions activeFocus true->false when the menu is dismissed, and onPressed now calls forceActiveFocus() redundantly.
changes: Replace the anonymous Qt.callLater arrow function in onActiveFocusChanged with a named method on mainTextArea (so Qt cancels the deferred call automatically if the item is destroyed) and only reset Plasmoid.status to ActiveStatus if it is currently AcceptingInputStatus.

Avoid setting Plasmoid.status = PlasmaCore.Types.AcceptingInputStatus on Qt.RightButton before contextMenu.popup() (or ensure status is released if the editor does not end up with activeFocus when the menu closes) so an auto-hide panel or keyboard focus is not left stuck when right-clicking an unfocused note and dismissing the menu.
Remove the redundant duplicate forceActiveFocus() calls in the Qt.RightButton and contextMenu.visible branches of onPressed.

reviews.text: The diagnosis holds against PanelView::refreshStatus(): a panel only accepts keyboard input once an applet sets AcceptingInputStatus, and it then forces focus onto the first focus-chain item, while the old onActiveFocusChanged could never bootstrap (no activeFocus in a WindowDoesNotAcceptFocus panel) and dropped back to ActiveStatus as soon as the panel became focusable. Requesting input on press and then forcing focus on the clicked editor, keeping the status while focused and releasing it via Qt.callLater so a note-to-note switch never toggles the containment status (and so never re-triggers the first-item focus), is the normal libplasma applet contract and fixes both the reporter's 'first note gets the input' and the rig's 'goes to KRunner' variants. The before/after video and screenshots are clear, and the regression list covers desktop notes, compact popup notes, Escape, the context menu and persistence. Minor: the callLater closure touches mainTextArea after a possible applet removal (harmless warning at worst), and PanelView's unconditional first-item focus is a separate rough edge that could be improved later.
